I’ll trace scorer reconstruction and guardrail loading, add the server-side execution boundary, and run focused tests using the provided environment. I’m using the repository’s Python style skill for this change.
Scorer reconstruction has an opt-in check, but still executes source inside the server when enabled. I’ll make server reconstruction return inert metadata and add a separate guardrail rejection that also catches custom scorers nested in ensembles.
The code now keeps custom scorers inert in the server and rejects them as guardrails during creation and loading. Executor permission uses process-local state, so an inherited environment variable cannot grant it. I’m adding tests for those boundaries, nested ensembles, and the named 500 error for existing guardrails.
The new reconstruction and guardrail-loading tests pass. Three existing trace-recording tests failed because no trace was recorded, and pytest’s resource-summary hook hit a sandbox permission error. I’m checking the workspace-aware creation tests next, along with ensemble behavior and server startup coverage.
All 131 focused tests passed, including guardrail creation with workspaces enabled and disabled. Built-in scorers and helper-created judges still reconstruct normally, and custom scorers can be rebuilt by the executor from inert server metadata. I’m rechecking the earlier trace failures in isolation.
Implemented inert custom-scorer reconstruction in the server, preserving metadata and serialization while refusing execution. Clients and job executors retain existing behavior; executor permission is process-local.

Custom guardrails—including ensembles—are rejected at creation and loading. Existing affected guardrails produce a named HTTP 500; other loading failures remain logged and skipped.

Validation: 131 focused tests passed, including workspace variants. Three additional trace-recording tests failed because no traces were recorded. No dependencies installed.

+import json
+from dataclasses import asdict, is_dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from mlflow.exceptions import MlflowException
+from mlflow.protos.databricks_pb2 import INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from mlflow.genai.scorers.base import SerializedScorer
+
+
+class CustomScorerGuardrailError(MlflowException):
+    def __init__(self, name: str):
+        super().__init__(
+            f"Guardrail '{name}' uses custom scorer code, which cannot run in the tracking server.",
+            error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
+        )
+
+
+def validate_guardrail_scorer(name: str, serialized_scorer: "str | dict | SerializedScorer") -> None:
+    from mlflow.genai.scorers.scorer_utils import _obj_has_call_source
+
+    data = json.loads(serialized_scorer) if isinstance(serialized_scorer, str) else serialized_scorer
+    if is_dataclass(data):
+        data = asdict(data)
+    if _obj_has_call_source(data):
+        raise CustomScorerGuardrailError(name)

+++ b/mlflow/utils/scorer_execution.py
@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+import sys
+
+# Process-local state: executor permission must never be inherited from environment variables.
+_is_server_process = False
+
+
+def is_server_process() -> bool:
+    flask = sys.modules.get("flask")
+    return _is_server_process or (flask is not None and flask.has_request_context())
+
+
+def mark_server_process() -> None:
+    global _is_server_process
+    _is_server_process = True
+
+
+def mark_job_executor_process() -> None:
+    global _is_server_process
+    _is_server_process = False
